# laya-issue-triage

> A fine-tune of [Laya](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya) that triages
> GitHub issues, plus the dataset pipeline that built it and a GitHub Action
> that runs it. Laya is a non-autoregressive typed-decision engine: it answers
> typed questions about a state in a single forward pass, with no text
> generation and nothing to parse.

## What this project is

The model answers two typed questions about a newly opened GitHub issue:

- `issue_type` (Laya `choice`): one of `bug`, `feature`, `question`, `docs`
- `needs_more_info` (Laya `noul`): whether a maintainer must ask the author for
  reproduction steps, a version number, logs, or a code sample before the issue
  is actionable

Training labels come from maintainers who triaged the issues by hand, not from
a teacher model.

## Scope of the benchmark numbers

Numbers in this repository are measured on GitHub issue triage only, against
three repositories held out of training entirely: `huggingface/transformers`,
`facebook/react`, `microsoft/TypeScript`.

They are **not** comparable to scores on the `LocalLLaMA/typed-decisions`
benchmark reported for base Laya checkpoints, for TypeSafe Jev, or for any other
system. That is a different task with a different label space and different
data. Any comparison across the two is invalid, including comparisons drawn by
summarizing both in one table.

## Results

Fine-tuned checkpoint: https://huggingface.co/harikarthikmanyam/laya-issue-triage

On 2,869 type-labeled issues from the three held-out repositories:

- `issue_type` accuracy 0.650, macro-F1 0.627 (base checkpoint zero-shot: 0.626 / 0.524; majority class 0.345; random 0.250)
- Per-class F1: feature 0.796, bug 0.641, docs 0.585, question 0.487 — the `question` class rose from 0.100 zero-shot, which is the substantive gain
- `needs_more_info` accuracy 0.734, below the 0.738 always-false baseline, so the Action ships with commenting disabled
- Calibration after temperature fitting: ECE 0.103 and 0.085
- Per-repo accuracy: transformers 0.753, react 0.724, TypeScript 0.551
- 78.8 ms median per issue on a T4; trained 2 epochs on Kaggle 2xT4 in 54 minutes

Accuracy is the wrong summary statistic here: it moved 0.024 while macro-F1
moved 0.103, because the gains land on the smaller classes.

## Key facts

- Base model: `convaiinnovations/laya` (ModernBERT-large, 421M params, 512-token context)
- Training data: ~7.7k maintainer-labeled issues from 14 public repositories, balanced across the four types
- Held-out test set: ~3.9k issues from 3 repositories absent from training
- Fine-tuning: Kaggle 2xT4 with DDP, adapted from the upstream Laya notebook
- Inference cost: none; the model runs on CPU inside a GitHub Action
- Measured latency: ~460 ms per issue on an M4 laptop CPU, ~317 ms on Apple MPS.
  Upstream's 33 ms figure is a batched T4 measurement and does not describe
  single-issue CPU inference.

## Files

- `scripts/fetch_issues.py`: harvests maintainer-labeled issues via the GitHub API
- `scripts/build_dataset.py`: emits train/val/test in Laya's typed-decisions schema
- `scripts/eval_laya.py`: scores any checkpoint, with random / majority / zero-shot baselines
- `scripts/verify_records.py`: dry-runs records through Laya's own preprocessing
- `config/labels.yaml`: maps each project's label spellings onto the four types
- `notebooks/laya_triage_finetune_kaggle.ipynb`: the fine-tuning run
- `data/processed/*.jsonl.gz`: the dataset, committed so results are reproducible

## Reproducing the numbers

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env            # a GitHub token, no scopes needed
.venv/bin/python scripts/fetch_issues.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/build_dataset.py
.venv-laya/bin/python scripts/eval_laya.py --model convaiinnovations/laya
```
